depart.text: Taoudenni at dawn: grey slabs of salt are stacked beside the kneeling camels. Three weeks of sand lie ahead. The old caravan master asks how you will load.
depart.speaker: keeper

choices.text: Five slabs on every camel, to earn the most
Four slabs and two spare water skins on each camel
Three slabs only, to travel light and fast

dunes.text: On the third day the wind lifts the sand and the dunes lose their shape. The track vanishes in a brown haze. The camels shuffle and look at you.
dunes.speaker: you

choices.text: Push on blindly and hope the camels know the way
Halt, shelter the camels, and steer by the stars when night falls

lost.text: You wander in circles for half a day and stop at the same bent thorn tree twice. Water skins grow light. At last the stars clear and you find the line again.

stars.text: You kneel the camels and wait. When night falls, the stars show the way, the cold wind eases and the caravan rests. By dawn, the track is plain again.

araouane.text: At Araouane the well-keeper asks you to settle shares. "Of every four slabs, one goes to the miners and three to the camel owners. Eight arrived. How many for the owners?"
araouane.speaker: keeper

puzzle.prompt: How many slabs go to the camel owners?

limp.text: Your strongest camel is limping, a stone caught in its foot, and you are still a week from the market. Its four slabs now seem to weigh a mountain.
limp.speaker: you

choices.text: Leave the camel and its slabs behind on the sand
Drive it on with a stick; it must keep pace
Take the stone out, share its slabs among the others and walk beside it

well.text: At the last well another caravan arrives at the same hour. The water is slow to rise and both sides have thirsty camels. Voices rise too.
well.speaker: rival

choices.text: Draw first, because you arrived first
Wait your turn quietly, and then trade a slab for extra water
Propose that the camels of both caravans drink in turns, counted together

market.text: Timbuktu at last. The buyer turns a slab in his hands and spots a crack. "Is this all good salt?" Some of your slabs broke in the long journey.
market.speaker: buyer

choices.text: Hide the cracked slabs between the sound ones
Refuse to sell until the price rises
Show the cracked slabs openly and sell them for a lower, fair price

home.text: The coins are counted, the camels are fed, and the road back is already in your mind. Behind you, a new line of grey slabs waits in the sun.

endings.headline: Salt, water and good name
endings.text: Every camel arrives, the shares are fair and your name opens every gate on the road.

endings.headline: A caravan that arrived
endings.text: The salt is sold and the camels are alive, though the road taught some hard lessons.

endings.headline: A lean arrival
endings.text: You reach the market thirsty, short of salt and short of friends.
